newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet crudes firm, forward values slip.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet crudes firm, forward values slip.

text.p: Benchmark Brent and other wet North Sea crudes were steady to firmer on Friday but forward paper markets pointed to softer values next week, traders said.
Dated Brent held the higher end of Thursday's range when cargoes traded 22 cents apart, with Aug 28-30 cargoes fetching broadly similar levels of Sept Brent -8 cents and Oct Brent -15 cents.

But some traders said the grade was heading for a fall having been propped up this week to boost a related swaps position. They pointed to Friday's clocking of the first September cargo to Cargill and big losses on Brent CFDs.
Brent CFDs for next week's Aug 18-22 dates traded at Oct Brent -26 cents, six cents weaker than early trade and cash intermonth spreads also backed off.
The Sept/Oct spread fetched -7 cents, five cents weaker than late on Thursday and Oct/Nov dipped to trade at -12 and -13 cents. Oct Brent on the IPE shed nine cents to $18.94 a barrel by 1530 GMT.
Elsewhere in the North Sea, sellers were drawing modest encouragement from evidence of thinner loadings next month.
Schedules released this week showed volumes from the 8 main export systems were expected to fall by 280,000 barrels per day.
Forties, which is expected to be about five cargoes lighter next month, was rumoured to have traded at Dated Brent +33/35 cents for an early September cargo, two or three cents better than last done.

Norwegian Oseberg, the only grade which should see higher volumes after returning from maintenance in August, also fetched a firmer premium as one million barrels due to load Sept 4-6 traded at Dated Brent +25 cents.
A late August cargo traded at +15 cents on Thursday.
